record.title: SonoBase paper reports ultrasound segmentation transfer across 15 held-out and external datasets
record.summary: A paper presents SonoCorpus, a collection of 53 public ultrasound datasets, and SonoBase, an interactive segmentation model adapted from SAM2 with a multi-resolution encoder. The authors report comparative results across eight held-out benchmark datasets and seven fully external datasets, plus selected clinical measurements derived from segmentations. The evaluation is retrospective; the paper calls for prospective validation and does not establish clinical deployment safety.
organizations: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence
Sheikh Tahnoon Bin Mohammed Medical City

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors introduce SonoCorpus, a resource of 53 public ultrasound datasets with 456,963 images/frames and 1,626,085 masks, and SonoBase, an interactive SAM2-derived segmentation model with a multi-resolution encoder.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across eight held-out benchmark datasets, authors report 74.4 point-prompt and 78.4 box-prompt mean IoU; across seven fully external datasets they report 64.5 and 79.8, respectively. These are retrospective author-run evaluations.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports selected derived measurement errors within stated inter-observer variability, including ejection-fraction error of 6.63%, fetal head-circumference error of 1.81 mm and gestational-age error of 1.2 days. This does not establish prospective clinical safety or outcomes.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Authors publicly released checkpoints, code, split indices, deduplication hashes and dataset manifests; this activation inspected linked documentation but did not execute or verify results.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent team reproduced held-out or external results.
The 53 constituent licenses, deduplication manifest and all archived per-sample outputs were not audited in this activation.
Retrospective benchmarks do not establish prospective safety, fairness or performance at new sites.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported transfer results replicate, pooling diverse ultrasound segmentation datasets into an interactive foundation model could reduce brittleness across organs, scanners, operators and geographies, with potential relevance to point-of-care and lower-resource settings. This could alter medical-imaging research priorities, while the evidence remains retrospective and is not deployment validation.
limitations: No independent reproduction or external audit was conducted in this activation.
All evaluations are retrospective; application-specific prospective validation is needed. SonoBase is described as a research tool, not a medical device.
Seven external datasets do not cover every scanner, population, application or acquisition protocol.
Demographic metadata are absent from nearly all source datasets, limiting subgroup analysis.
A zero-shot box-prompt abdominal-circumference endpoint on ACOUSLIC favors a baseline; the authors report calibration/few-shot adaptation changes this comparison, which needs validation.
Dataset licenses are heterogeneous; some restrict non-commercial use, and model weights have a non-commercial restriction.

brief.summary: A paper presents SonoCorpus, a collection of 53 public ultrasound datasets, and SonoBase, an interactive segmentation model adapted from SAM2 with a multi-resolution encoder. The authors report comparative results across eight held-out benchmark datasets and seven fully external datasets, plus selected clinical measurements derived from segmentations. The evaluation is retrospective; the paper calls for prospective validation and does not establish clinical deployment safety.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report point/box mIoU 74.4/78.4 across 8 benchmark datasets and 64.5/79.8 across 7 external datasets; selected derived measures include EF error 6.63%, fetal head circumference 1.81 mm and gestational age 1.2 days.
technical.demonstrated_result: Primary preprint, code, checkpoint and dataset manifest are publicly referenced. This activation did not execute model or independently reproduce scores.
technical.mechanism: Replaces SAM2 image encoder with a hybrid multi-resolution encoder: Hiera transformer for low-resolution context and two ConvNeXt branches for medium/high-resolution detail, joined by cross-branch attention. Retains prompt and memory modules.
technical.regime: 53 datasets across 24 applications, 17 countries and 2D/video/3D modalities. Training uses 38 pretraining datasets plus training partitions from 8 benchmark datasets; 7 external datasets are fully withheld. Retrospective tests.
technical.strongest_baseline: SAM2, MedSAM2, task-specific specialists and separate MedSAM3 comparisons. Results vary by prompt and evaluation regime; one external abdominal-circumference endpoint favors a baseline before calibration.

brief.title: SonoBase paper reports ultrasound segmentation transfer across 15 held-out and external datasets
brief.why_it_matters: Ultrasound models can lose accuracy when scanner, operator, anatomy or acquisition conditions change. The paper tests whether ultrasound-specific pretraining over a diverse public corpus improves interactive segmentation across such shifts, including handheld devices and lower-resource settings.
